meta.title: Tech Landscape
meta.subtitle: Software & AI infrastructure, mapped
meta.note: Market caps from companiesmarketcap.com (Nov 21, 2026); private companies show last reported valuation with its date. Verify before relying on them.

tree.name: Software & AI Infrastructure
tree.desc: Two branches: AI (chips → models → AI infrastructure → AI apps) and Software (cloud, data, devtools, security, business apps). Click any branch to expand it.

children.name: AI
children.desc: The AI stack, bottom to top: compute and hardware → models → the infrastructure to train, serve and evaluate them → AI applications and agents.

children.name: AI Compute & Hardware
children.desc: The physical layer of AI: the chips that do the math, the memory and networking that feed them, and the data centers and power that house them. Most AI spending ultimately lands here.

children.name: GPUs & AI Accelerators
children.desc: Chips that run the matrix math behind training and inference. Nvidia dominates with GPUs + CUDA software; everyone else is trying to beat it on cost, speed or power.

children.name: Nvidia
children.desc: Dominant AI chipmaker — GPUs (Hopper, Blackwell, Rubin) plus the CUDA software ecosystem that locks developers in. Also sells networking and full rack-scale systems.

children.name: AMD
children.desc: Main merchant-GPU rival to Nvidia with its Instinct MI-series accelerators and ROCm software; also makes server CPUs (EPYC).

children.name: Broadcom
children.desc: Designs custom AI chips (ASICs) for hyperscalers like Google (TPU) and Meta, and sells Ethernet switch chips. Also owns VMware.

children.name: Marvell
children.desc: Custom AI silicon and data-center networking/optical chips; designs custom accelerators for Amazon and others.

children.name: Intel
children.desc: Legacy CPU giant (Xeon) with Gaudi AI accelerators and a foundry business it is trying to rebuild.

children.name: Arm
children.desc: Licenses the CPU architecture used in nearly every phone and increasingly in data-center chips (Nvidia Grace, AWS Graviton). Majority-owned by SoftBank.

children.name: Cerebras
children.desc: Makes wafer-scale AI chips (one chip the size of a dinner plate) and sells very fast inference. IPO'd May 2026 — the largest AI IPO ever at the time.

children.name: Groq
children.desc: Built the LPU, a chip designed for ultra-fast inference. Nvidia struck a ~$20B licensing and talent deal with Groq in late 2025.

children.name: SambaNova
children.desc: AI chips and full-stack systems aimed at enterprise inference.

children.name: Tenstorrent
children.desc: RISC-V-based AI chips and IP led by chip legend Jim Keller; sells hardware and licenses designs.

children.name: Etched
children.desc: Building Sohu, a chip hard-wired for transformer models — a bet that one architecture wins.

children.name: d-Matrix
children.desc: In-memory compute chips for low-cost, low-latency inference.

children.name: Memory, Foundry & Chip Supply Chain
children.desc: Who actually manufactures the chips. AI chips need cutting-edge fabs (TSMC), lithography machines (ASML) and stacked high-bandwidth memory (HBM) — all serious bottlenecks.

children.name: TSMC
children.desc: World's leading contract chip manufacturer; fabricates nearly every advanced AI chip, including Nvidia's and Apple's, plus advanced packaging (CoWoS).

children.name: ASML
children.desc: Monopoly maker of EUV lithography machines needed to print the most advanced chips.

children.name: SK hynix
children.desc: Leading supplier of HBM memory stacked next to AI GPUs. Added a US listing in 2026.

children.name: Micron
children.desc: US memory maker (DRAM, HBM, NAND) — a key HBM supplier.

children.name: Samsung Electronics
children.desc: Memory giant and second-largest foundry; racing to catch up in HBM.

children.name: Synopsys
children.desc: Electronic design automation (EDA) software used to design chips; acquired Ansys (simulation) in 2025.

children.name: Cadence
children.desc: The other big EDA vendor — chip design software and hardware emulation.

children.name: Networking & Interconnect
children.desc: Training runs span tens of thousands of chips that must talk constantly. Switches, optics and interconnect chips are a fast-growing piece of AI capex.

children.name: Arista Networks
children.desc: High-speed Ethernet switches for cloud and AI data centers.

children.name: Astera Labs
children.desc: Connectivity chips (PCIe/CXL retimers, switches) that link GPUs, CPUs and memory.

children.name: Credo
children.desc: High-speed connectivity — active electrical cables and SerDes for AI clusters.

children.name: Coherent
children.desc: Optical transceivers and lasers for data-center links.

children.name: Lightmatter
children.desc: Photonic (light-based) interconnect for AI chips.

children.name: Ayar Labs
children.desc: Optical I/O chiplets to move data between chips with light instead of copper.

children.name: Data Centers, Power & Cooling
children.desc: AI is now power-constrained. Data-center developers, power equipment makers and cooling vendors sit where tech meets energy and industrials.

children.name: Equinix
children.desc: Largest colocation/interconnection data-center REIT globally.

children.name: Digital Realty
children.desc: Large data-center REIT leasing wholesale capacity to hyperscalers.

children.name: Aligned Data Centers
children.desc: Hyperscale data-center developer; agreed to a ~$40B sale to a consortium including BlackRock/GIP, MGX and the AI Infrastructure Partnership.

children.name: Vantage Data Centers
children.desc: Hyperscale campus developer (backed by DigitalBridge).

children.name: QTS
children.desc: Hyperscale data-center operator taken private by Blackstone in 2021.

children.name: Vertiv
children.desc: Power and thermal management (UPS, liquid cooling) for data centers.

children.name: Schneider Electric
children.desc: Electrical distribution, power management and cooling for data centers.

children.name: Eaton
children.desc: Power distribution and electrical equipment — switchgear, UPS — for data centers and grids.

children.name: GE Vernova
children.desc: Gas turbines, grid equipment and wind; benefiting from data-center power demand.

children.name: Oklo
children.desc: Developing small fast-fission nuclear reactors pitched as power for data centers.

children.name: GPU Clouds (Neoclouds)
children.desc: Specialist clouds that rent GPUs by the hour, usually cheaper or faster to get than AWS/Azure. Heavily debt-financed, with big contracts from AI labs.

children.name: CoreWeave
children.desc: Largest neocloud; rents Nvidia GPU capacity to OpenAI, Microsoft and others. IPO'd 2025; bought Weights & Biases.

children.name: Nebius
children.desc: Amsterdam-based AI cloud spun out of Yandex; large Microsoft capacity deal.

children.name: Lambda
children.desc: GPU cloud and on-prem GPU servers popular with AI researchers.

children.name: Crusoe
children.desc: AI cloud and data-center developer building campuses near cheap/stranded energy (e.g. the Abilene, TX Stargate site).

children.name: Together AI
children.desc: GPU cloud plus serverless inference and fine-tuning for open models.

children.name: Vultr
children.desc: Independent cloud provider with a growing GPU offering.

children.name: Fluidstack
children.desc: GPU cloud building large clusters for AI labs.

children.name: RunPod
children.desc: Developer-friendly GPU cloud with serverless GPU endpoints.

children.name: AI Models
children.desc: The labs training frontier models — language, multimodal, image, video, voice — and the hubs where open models are shared.

children.name: Foundation Model Labs
children.desc: Companies training frontier large language and multimodal models — the most capital-intensive part of software.

children.name: OpenAI
children.desc: Maker of GPT models and ChatGPT; restructured into a public benefit corporation; has said it will not IPO in 2026.

children.name: Anthropic
children.desc: Maker of Claude models and Claude Code; listed on Nasdaq (ANT) in Nov 2026 at a ~$1.2T valuation.

children.name: Google DeepMind
children.desc: Google's AI lab; builds Gemini models.

children.name: Meta AI
children.desc: Meta's AI division — open-weight Llama models and Meta Superintelligence Labs.

children.name: xAI
children.desc: Elon Musk's lab behind Grok; merged into SpaceX in 2026.

children.name: Mistral AI
children.desc: Paris-based lab with open-weight and commercial models; Europe's AI champion.

children.name: Cohere
children.desc: Toronto lab focused on enterprise models, search (embeddings/rerank) and private deployment.

children.name: DeepSeek
children.desc: Chinese lab whose cheap, strong open-weight models (R1) shocked markets in early 2025.

children.name: Thinking Machines Lab
children.desc: Lab founded by ex-OpenAI CTO Mira Murati.

children.name: Safe Superintelligence
children.desc: Ilya Sutskever's lab focused solely on safe superintelligence.

children.name: Reflection AI
children.desc: Building open frontier models in the US.

children.name: Generative Media Models
children.desc: Models that generate images, video, voice and music.

children.name: Runway
children.desc: AI video generation and editing tools used in film and advertising.

children.name: Black Forest Labs
children.desc: German lab behind the FLUX image models.

children.name: Midjourney
children.desc: Popular image (and video) generator; famously bootstrapped.

children.name: ElevenLabs
children.desc: AI voice — text-to-speech, voice cloning, dubbing and voice agents.

children.name: Suno
children.desc: AI music generation.

children.name: Luma AI
children.desc: Video and 3D generation models.

children.name: World Labs
children.desc: Fei-Fei Li's company building 3D 'world models'; AMD agreed to buy it in late 2026.

children.name: Model Hubs & Open-Source Tooling
children.desc: Where open models are shared and the frameworks used to build them.

children.name: Hugging Face
children.desc: The 'GitHub of AI' — hosts millions of open models and datasets. Nvidia agreed to buy it for ~$12.9B in Sept 2026.

children.name: PyTorch
children.desc: Dominant deep learning framework, created at Meta; now under the Linux Foundation.

children.name: vLLM
children.desc: Leading open-source LLM inference engine.

children.name: Ollama
children.desc: Run open models locally on your laptop.

children.name: AI Infrastructure
children.desc: The tooling between the chips and the apps: training data, training and MLOps, inference serving, vector databases, frameworks, agent infrastructure, evaluation and AI security.

children.name: Training Data & Labeling
children.desc: Human experts and synthetic data that teach models. Post-training (RLHF, reasoning data) made expert labelers a big business.

children.name: Scale AI
children.desc: Data labeling and evaluation for AI labs and the US government; Meta bought 49% in 2025 and hired its CEO.

children.name: Surge AI
children.desc: High-skill human data for RLHF; profitable and bootstrapped.

children.name: Mercor
children.desc: Marketplace of domain experts (lawyers, doctors, bankers) hired to train AI models.

children.name: Snorkel AI
children.desc: Programmatic data labeling and expert data for model evaluation.

children.name: Labelbox
children.desc: Labeling platform and expert data network.

children.name: Turing
children.desc: Coding and reasoning data for frontier labs.

children.name: Mostly AI
children.desc: Synthetic tabular data generation.

children.name: Training, Fine-Tuning & MLOps
children.desc: Software to train and fine-tune models, track experiments and manage the ML lifecycle.

children.name: Weights & Biases
children.desc: Experiment tracking and model management used by most AI labs.

children.name: Modular
children.desc: Mojo language and MAX engine to run AI across any hardware — a bet against CUDA lock-in.

children.name: Anyscale
children.desc: Company behind Ray, the open-source framework for distributed AI compute.

children.name: Unsloth
children.desc: Fast, memory-efficient open-source fine-tuning.

children.name: Comet
children.desc: Experiment tracking and LLM evaluation (Opik).

children.name: MLflow
children.desc: Open-source ML lifecycle platform.

children.name: Inference & Model Serving
children.desc: Running models in production — fast, cheap and reliable. As usage explodes, inference is becoming the biggest AI compute bill.

children.name: Fireworks AI
children.desc: Fast inference platform for open models, from ex-PyTorch leads at Meta.

children.name: Baseten
children.desc: Inference platform for deploying custom and open models.

children.name: Modal
children.desc: Serverless GPU compute — run Python functions on GPUs instantly.

children.name: Replicate
children.desc: Run open models through a simple API.

children.name: fal
children.desc: Generative media inference platform (image, video, audio).

children.name: OpenRouter
children.desc: One API that routes requests across hundreds of models and providers.

children.name: Vector Databases & Retrieval
children.desc: Stores 'embeddings' (numeric meaning of text/images) so AI apps can find relevant context — the core of RAG (retrieval-augmented generation).

children.name: Pinecone
children.desc: Managed, serverless vector database.

children.name: Weaviate
children.desc: Open-source vector database.

children.name: Zilliz (Milvus)
children.desc: Company behind Milvus, a widely used open-source vector database.

children.name: Chroma
children.desc: Open-source embedding database popular with developers.

children.name: Qdrant
children.desc: Open-source vector search engine written in Rust.

children.name: turbopuffer
children.desc: Cheap vector + full-text search built on object storage (used by Cursor, Notion).

children.name: LanceDB
children.desc: Multimodal AI database built on the Lance file format.

children.name: LLM Frameworks & RAG
children.desc: Developer frameworks for chaining models, tools and data into apps and agents.

children.name: LangChain
children.desc: Most popular LLM app framework, plus LangGraph (agents) and LangSmith (observability).

children.name: LlamaIndex
children.desc: Framework and cloud for document parsing and RAG over enterprise data.

children.name: Contextual AI
children.desc: Enterprise RAG platform from the researchers who coined RAG.

children.name: Unstructured
children.desc: Turns messy documents (PDFs, slides) into AI-ready data.

children.name: deepset
children.desc: Company behind Haystack, an open-source RAG framework.

children.name: Agent Infrastructure
children.desc: The plumbing AI agents need to act: sandboxes to run code, browsers to use websites, memory, tool connections and web search.

children.name: E2B
children.desc: Secure cloud sandboxes where AI agents run code.

children.name: Browserbase
children.desc: Headless browsers in the cloud for AI agents.

children.name: Composio
children.desc: Connects agents to hundreds of apps and APIs.

children.name: Letta
children.desc: Stateful agents with long-term memory (from the MemGPT research).

children.name: Mem0
children.desc: Memory layer for AI apps and agents.

children.name: Exa
children.desc: Web search API built for AI.

children.name: Firecrawl
children.desc: Turns websites into clean data for LLMs.

children.name: Daytona
children.desc: Infrastructure for running AI-generated code.

children.name: LLM Evaluation & Observability
children.desc: Testing and monitoring AI apps — catching hallucinations, regressions and cost spikes. Hot M&A area in 2026 as incumbents bought in.

children.name: Braintrust
children.desc: Evals and observability platform for AI products.

children.name: Arize AI
children.desc: ML and LLM observability; Dynatrace closed the ~$915M deal in Oct 2026.

children.name: Galileo
children.desc: AI agent evaluation and observability; now Splunk Agent Observability.

children.name: Langfuse
children.desc: Open-source LLM tracing and evals.

children.name: Patronus AI
children.desc: Automated evaluation of LLM outputs.

children.name: Helicone
children.desc: Open-source LLM observability and gateway.

children.name: AI Security & Governance
children.desc: Protecting models and agents from prompt injection, data leaks and misuse, and documenting compliance.

children.name: Protect AI
children.desc: Security for the ML supply chain and LLM apps.

children.name: Lakera
children.desc: Defends LLM apps against prompt injection.

children.name: HiddenLayer
children.desc: Security platform for AI models.

children.name: Credo AI
children.desc: AI governance and risk management.

children.name: AI Applications & Agents
children.desc: The top of the stack — products people and businesses use directly. Where AI usage (and the revenue that funds everything below) shows up.

children.name: Assistants & Search
children.desc: General-purpose chat assistants and AI search.

children.name: ChatGPT
children.desc: The most-used AI assistant.

children.name: Claude
children.desc: Anthropic's assistant, strong in coding and work tasks.

children.name: Gemini
children.desc: Google's assistant, built into Android and Workspace.

children.name: Perplexity
children.desc: AI answer engine and Comet browser.

children.name: Character.AI
children.desc: Chat with custom AI characters.

children.name: AI Coding Tools
children.desc: AI that writes, reviews and ships code — the fastest-growing software category of 2025–26.

children.name: Cursor
children.desc: AI-first code editor from Anysphere; SpaceX bought it for $60B in stock, closing Aug 2026.

children.name: GitHub Copilot
children.desc: The original mainstream AI coding assistant.

children.name: Claude Code
children.desc: Anthropic's agentic coding tool that runs in the terminal and IDE.

children.name: Cognition
children.desc: Maker of Devin (autonomous AI engineer); also owns Windsurf's IDE business.

children.name: Replit
children.desc: Browser IDE with an agent that builds and deploys full apps.

children.name: Lovable
children.desc: Stockholm-based 'vibe coding' app builder — describe an app, get it built.

children.name: Bolt (StackBlitz)
children.desc: In-browser AI app builder.

children.name: JetBrains
children.desc: IntelliJ and other professional IDEs, plus AI assistants.

children.name: Customer Support Agents
children.desc: AI agents that resolve customer tickets end-to-end — one of the first AI categories with clear ROI.

children.name: Sierra
children.desc: Conversational AI agents for customer experience, co-founded by Bret Taylor.

children.name: Decagon
children.desc: AI customer support agents for enterprises.

children.name: Parloa
children.desc: AI voice agents for contact centers.

children.name: Ada
children.desc: AI customer service automation.

children.name: Enterprise Search & Knowledge
children.desc: AI that searches and reasons across a company's internal documents.

children.name: Glean
children.desc: Enterprise AI search and assistant across company apps.

children.name: Writer
children.desc: Enterprise generative AI platform with its own models.

children.name: Creative & Content
children.desc: AI for video, avatars, presentations and design.

children.name: HeyGen
children.desc: AI avatar videos and translation.

children.name: Synthesia
children.desc: AI video for corporate training and communications.

children.name: Gamma
children.desc: AI presentations and documents.

children.name: Software
children.desc: Traditional software: cloud and infrastructure, data, developer tools, security, and the business applications companies run on. Most of it is now adding AI.

children.name: Cloud & Infrastructure Software
children.desc: Renting compute, storage and networking instead of owning servers, plus the software used to run and automate that infrastructure.

children.name: Hyperscalers
children.desc: The giant public clouds. They sell everything from raw VMs to AI models, and are the biggest buyers of AI chips.

children.name: Amazon Web Services
children.desc: Largest cloud by revenue; also designs its own chips (Trainium, Graviton) and is a major Anthropic partner.

children.name: Microsoft Azure
children.desc: #2 cloud; hosts OpenAI's models and sells them via Azure AI Foundry.

children.name: Google Cloud
children.desc: #3 cloud; strong in data (BigQuery) and AI with in-house TPUs and Gemini. Now owns Wiz.

children.name: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure
children.desc: Smaller but fast-growing cloud that has won huge AI capacity contracts (OpenAI/Stargate).

children.name: Alibaba Cloud
children.desc: Largest cloud in China; also develops the Qwen open models.

children.name: Developer Clouds & PaaS
children.desc: Simpler platforms where developers deploy apps without managing servers. Lots of AI-native apps start here.

children.name: Vercel
children.desc: Frontend cloud and creator of Next.js; also makes v0, an AI app builder.

children.name: Netlify
children.desc: Platform for deploying web frontends and serverless functions.

children.name: Render
children.desc: Simple cloud for web services, databases and background jobs.

children.name: Railway
children.desc: Instant-deploy app hosting popular with indie developers.

children.name: Fly.io
children.desc: Runs apps close to users on servers worldwide.

children.name: DigitalOcean
children.desc: Developer- and SMB-focused cloud, now adding GPU droplets.

children.name: Heroku
children.desc: Pioneering PaaS, owned by Salesforce.

children.name: Edge, CDN & Networking
children.desc: Networks that sit between users and apps — caching content, blocking attacks and running code close to users.

children.name: Cloudflare
children.desc: Global network for CDN, security (DDoS, zero trust) and edge compute; bought Replicate (AI model hosting) in 2025.

children.name: Akamai
children.desc: Original CDN; now also security and cloud compute (Linode).

children.name: Fastly
children.desc: Edge cloud/CDN with programmable edge compute.

children.name: Kong
children.desc: API gateway and service connectivity platform, now with AI gateway features.

children.name: Containers & Kubernetes
children.desc: Containers package an app with everything it needs; Kubernetes runs thousands of them across machines. The default way to run modern software.

children.name: Docker
children.desc: Created the container standard; sells developer tools (Docker Desktop, Hub).

children.name: Kubernetes
children.desc: Open-source container orchestrator originally from Google; managed by every cloud.

children.name: Red Hat
children.desc: Enterprise Linux and OpenShift (Kubernetes platform); acquired by IBM for $34B in 2019.

children.name: SUSE
children.desc: Enterprise Linux and Rancher (Kubernetes management); taken private by EQT.

children.name: Infrastructure as Code & Platform Engineering
children.desc: Defining cloud infrastructure in code files so it can be versioned and automated, plus internal portals that let developers self-serve.

children.name: HashiCorp
children.desc: Terraform (infrastructure as code) and Vault (secrets management).

children.name: OpenTofu
children.desc: Community fork of Terraform after HashiCorp changed its license.

children.name: Pulumi
children.desc: Infrastructure as code using real programming languages.

children.name: Spacelift
children.desc: Orchestration and governance for Terraform/OpenTofu workflows.

children.name: Port
children.desc: Internal developer portal for platform engineering teams.

children.name: Virtualization, Storage & Backup
children.desc: The traditional enterprise data-center stack — virtual machines, storage arrays and backup — still huge, and being reshaped by AI data needs.

children.name: VMware
children.desc: Dominant server virtualization software; acquired by Broadcom for $69B in 2023, followed by big price increases.

children.name: Nutanix
children.desc: Hyperconverged infrastructure; a beneficiary of customers leaving VMware.

children.name: NetApp
children.desc: Enterprise storage and data management across on-prem and cloud.

children.name: Pure Storage
children.desc: All-flash storage arrays, sold increasingly as a subscription.

children.name: VAST Data
children.desc: Storage and data platform built for AI training and inference at scale.

children.name: Rubrik
children.desc: Backup and cyber-recovery with data security posture management.

children.name: Cohesity
children.desc: Backup and data security; merged with Veritas' data protection business in 2024.

children.name: Veeam
children.desc: Backup and recovery software; acquired Securiti AI (data security) for $1.7B in 2025.

children.name: Data Infrastructure
children.desc: How companies collect, move, store, clean and analyze data. This was the 'modern data stack' — now being rebuilt as the foundation for AI.

children.name: Operational Databases (OLTP)
children.desc: Databases behind live apps — every login, order or payment writes here. OLTP = online transaction processing: many small, fast reads and writes.

children.name: Oracle Database
children.desc: The incumbent enterprise relational database, still running most big banks and ERPs.

children.name: MongoDB
children.desc: Leading document (NoSQL) database; Atlas is its managed cloud service.

children.name: PostgreSQL
children.desc: The most popular open-source relational database; many startups sell hosted Postgres.

children.name: Microsoft SQL Server
children.desc: Microsoft's relational database, common in enterprises.

children.name: Amazon Aurora & DynamoDB
children.desc: AWS's managed relational (Aurora) and key-value (DynamoDB) databases.

children.name: Supabase
children.desc: Open-source backend built on Postgres (auth, storage, APIs) — popular with AI app builders.

children.name: Neon
children.desc: Serverless Postgres that spins up instantly; bought by Databricks for ~$1B.

children.name: PlanetScale
children.desc: Managed MySQL (Vitess) and Postgres built for scale.

children.name: CockroachDB
children.desc: Distributed SQL database that survives data-center failures.

children.name: Redis
children.desc: In-memory data store used for caching and real-time apps.

children.name: Couchbase
children.desc: NoSQL document database for enterprise apps.

children.name: DataStax
children.desc: Commercial Apache Cassandra and vector search.

children.name: SingleStore
children.desc: Database that handles both transactions and analytics in real time.

children.name: Warehouses & Lakehouses (OLAP)
children.desc: Where companies store data for analytics and AI. A warehouse is structured and SQL-first; a lakehouse adds cheap open files on object storage. Snowflake vs. Databricks is the defining rivalry.

children.name: Snowflake
children.desc: Cloud data warehouse with usage-based pricing; expanding into AI (Cortex) and Postgres; acquired Observe in 2026.

children.name: Databricks
children.desc: Lakehouse platform born from Apache Spark; Snowflake's main rival. Valued ~$134B in early 2026 and said it won't IPO in 2026.

children.name: Google BigQuery
children.desc: Google Cloud's serverless data warehouse.

children.name: Amazon Redshift
children.desc: AWS's data warehouse.

children.name: Microsoft Fabric
children.desc: Microsoft's unified analytics platform combining warehouse, lake and Power BI.

children.name: ClickHouse
children.desc: Very fast open-source analytics database; acquired Langfuse (LLM observability).

children.name: MotherDuck
children.desc: Cloud service built on DuckDB, the lightweight in-process analytics database.

children.name: Starburst
children.desc: Query engine (Trino) that queries data where it lives without moving it.

children.name: Dremio
children.desc: Lakehouse query engine built around Apache Iceberg.

children.name: Firebolt
children.desc: Cloud warehouse tuned for low-latency analytics.

children.name: Open Table Formats & Object Storage
children.desc: Lakehouses keep data as open files on cheap object storage. Table formats like Iceberg add database features (updates, versions) on top, so any engine can read the same data.

children.name: Apache Iceberg
children.desc: Open table format created at Netflix; the industry is converging on it.

children.name: Delta Lake
children.desc: Databricks' open table format.

children.name: Tabular
children.desc: Founded by Iceberg's creators; bought by Databricks for ~$1–2B.

children.name: Onehouse
children.desc: Managed lakehouse built on Apache Hudi, compatible with Iceberg and Delta.

children.name: Amazon S3
children.desc: The default object store where most data lakes live.

children.name: MinIO
children.desc: S3-compatible object storage you can run anywhere.

children.name: Streaming & Real-Time Data
children.desc: Moving data continuously as events happen (a click, a trade, a sensor reading) instead of in nightly batches. Kafka is the standard.

children.name: Confluent
children.desc: Commercial company behind Apache Kafka; IBM closed its ~$11B acquisition in March 2026.

children.name: Apache Kafka
children.desc: The standard open-source event streaming platform, created at LinkedIn.

children.name: Apache Flink
children.desc: Open-source engine for processing streams (joins, aggregations) in real time.

children.name: Redpanda
children.desc: Kafka-compatible streaming platform rewritten in C++ for speed.

children.name: StreamNative
children.desc: Managed Apache Pulsar and Kafka-compatible streaming.

children.name: Materialize
children.desc: Streaming database that keeps SQL query results always up to date.

children.name: Data Integration (ETL/ELT)
children.desc: Pipelines that extract data from apps (Salesforce, databases) and load it into the warehouse, then transform it into clean tables.

children.name: Fivetran + dbt Labs
children.desc: Fivetran (managed connectors that load data) merged with dbt Labs (SQL transformations) in June 2026 — together the core of the modern data stack.

children.name: dbt
children.desc: The standard tool for transforming warehouse data with version-controlled SQL.

children.name: Airbyte
children.desc: Open-source data integration with hundreds of connectors.

children.name: Informatica
children.desc: Legacy enterprise data integration and management leader; acquired by Salesforce for ~$8B.

children.name: Matillion
children.desc: Cloud ETL built for Snowflake, Databricks and Redshift.

children.name: Coalesce
children.desc: Visual, column-aware data transformation for Snowflake and Databricks.

children.name: Hightouch
children.desc: Reverse ETL — pushes warehouse data back into marketing and sales tools.

children.name: Boomi
children.desc: Integration platform as a service (iPaaS) connecting enterprise apps.

children.name: MuleSoft
